rationale: Hall defines Dedekind, monotone, Cantor/nested-interval, Bolzano-Weierstrass, and sequential Cauchy completeness for ordered fields. The local definition selects five of these, uses the shrinking sequential NIP convention, and packages ARCH alongside them.

Lebl gives uniqueness, order preservation, convergent-implies-Cauchy, boundedness, and convergence from a convergent subsequence in the real case. The local item transfers and bundles the same elementary estimates for an arbitrary ordered field.

Hall records Dedekind completeness, Cantor completeness, and Archimedeanness in the ordered-field completeness framework. The local statement specializes the implication and notes that LUB proves the unrestricted interval form.

Hall establishes equivalence of Cantor/nested-interval and Bolzano-Weierstrass completeness for Archimedean ordered fields. The local NIP is the shrinking sequential convention and the proof expands the bisection construction.

Hall treats Bolzano-Weierstrass completeness as one of the equivalent completeness properties of Archimedean ordered fields and analyzes failures outside that setting. The local item isolates the standard fact that BW itself forces ARCH.

Hall gives Bolzano-Weierstrass and sequential Cauchy completeness in the same ordered-field equivalence theorem. The local item isolates the BW-to-CC implication and proves it through a convergent subsequence.
Hall states the equivalence of sequential Cauchy and monotone completeness in Archimedean ordered fields. The local theorem exposes ARCH and supplies a dependency-adapted increment argument.

Hall defines monotone completeness in the ordered-field setting and places it in the Archimedean completeness equivalence. The local item isolates the standard canonical-naturals contradiction showing MCT forces ARCH.

Hall states monotone and Dedekind completeness as equivalent for Archimedean ordered fields. The local statement keeps an explicitly redundant ARCH hypothesis and constructs the supremum by bisection.

Hall Theorem 3.11 gives equivalence of Dedekind, monotone, Cantor, Bolzano-Weierstrass, and sequential completeness for Archimedean ordered fields. The local theorem repackages exactly the five selected clauses so ARCH is attached only to NIP and CC.
The Encyclopedia of Mathematics defines the arithmetic averages (s_0+...+s_n)/(n+1) and summability by their limit. This matches the local zero-based definition and direction.
The source states Cauchy’s theorem that s_n tending to s implies its arithmetic averages tend to s, with the same quantifiers and conclusion. The numbered head-tail proof is local.

The source gives the infinity-over-infinity Stolz-Cesaro theorem for a strictly increasing unbounded denominator and convergent difference quotient. The local version changes indexing and states the conclusion on a positive tail to admit b_0=0.
The source gives the zero-over-zero Stolz-Cesaro form with a strictly decreasing positive denominator tending to zero. The local corollary uses zero-based indexing and expands the endpoint telescope.

The sources define matrix summation transforms, regularity, and the row/column conditions. The local definition restricts to finite row support so every transform is a finite sum and makes admissible row bounds explicit.
The Encyclopedia of Mathematics states the same three necessary and sufficient regularity conditions. The local theorem specializes to row-finite real matrices and numbers rows and columns from zero.
The sources identify Cesaro averaging as a matrix summation method and give the three regularity conditions. The local corollary verifies them for the zero-based row-finite Cesaro matrix.

This is exactly the local eventual-positive-infinity order; the local proof expands representative independence and the infinitesimal 1/t.
